criteria.name: SPFx runtime dependencies at 1.22.0
criteria.instructions: Check that all @microsoft/sp-* packages listed in package.json dependencies are upgraded to version 1.22.0. This includes @microsoft/sp-core-library, @microsoft/sp-webpart-base, @microsoft/sp-property-pane, @microsoft/sp-office-ui-fabric-core, and @microsoft/decorators. Other packages like @microsoft/sp-lodash-subset, @microsoft/sp-dialog, @microsoft/sp-http, @microsoft/sp-component-base, @microsoft/sp-diagnostics, @microsoft/sp-dynamic-data, @microsoft/sp-loader, @microsoft/sp-module-interfaces, @microsoft/sp-odata-types, @microsoft/sp-page-context, and @microsoft/sp-list-subscription should also be at 1.22.0 if present, but their absence is acceptable as they are optional. Packages specific to extensions (@microsoft/sp-application-base, @microsoft/sp-extension-base, @microsoft/sp-listview-extensibility) and ACEs (@microsoft/sp-adaptive-card-extension-base) are not expected in a webpart project and their absence should not count as a failure.

create.proposal: Create an 'spfx-upgrade' skill that provides a comprehensive, version-aware checklist for SPFx upgrades. For the 1.21→1.22 (Gulp-to-Heft) migration, the skill should enumerate ALL required changes: (1) uninstall gulp dependencies, (2) install heft dependencies including css-loader@7.1.2, (3) add rig.json, (4) replace sass.json with sass.json for heft, (5) add typescript.json, (6) replace tsconfig.json, (7) delete gulpfile.js, (8) update .yo-rc.json version to 1.22.0 and set useGulp to false, (9) remove 'main' property from package.json, (10) add scripts.start ('heft start --clean') and scripts.eject-webpack ('heft eject-webpack') as REQUIRED entries, (11) add resolutions for @types/react and overrides for @rushstack/heft, (12) remove src/index.ts, (13) update .gitignore for heft output directories, (14) update eslint config, (15) upgrade production SPFx packages. The skill should explicitly mark each step as required or optional and provide validation checks the agent can run after completing the migration.
create.rationale: The external Microsoft documentation proved incomplete (missing 8+ steps) and misleading (marking required scripts as optional). Since this is an external dependency we cannot directly control, a profile-owned skill provides a reliable, comprehensive, and version-specific source of truth. The skill can be updated immediately when new SPFx versions are released, without waiting for Microsoft to update their docs. This directly addresses both the ResponseFormat and MissingGroundingContent root causes.

create.gap: No instructions to supplement external docs with validation checks
create.behaviorChain: Agent treated the fetched migration guide as a complete and sufficient source of truth, never cross-checking against project artifacts (.yo-rc.json, .gitignore, src/index.ts) or performing post-migration validation. Instructions could prompt the agent to verify completeness.
create.proposal: Add a profile-level instruction that directs the agent, after completing any framework upgrade, to: (1) diff all config files (.yo-rc.json, package.json, tsconfig.json, .gitignore) against known upgrade expectations, (2) verify no stale artifacts remain (e.g., gulpfile.js, src/index.ts for heft migrations), (3) run the build to confirm the upgrade compiles, and (4) check that version references in metadata files match the target version. This 'verify after upgrade' instruction acts as a safety net when external documentation is incomplete.
create.rationale: Even with an SPFx upgrade skill, a general-purpose post-upgrade validation instruction provides defense-in-depth for any framework migration scenario. It would have caught the .yo-rc.json version mismatch, the leftover src/index.ts, and the missing .gitignore entries regardless of documentation quality.

constraints.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 training data likely predates SPFx v1.22.0 (released December 2025), so the model cannot supplement incomplete external documentation with its own knowledge of version-specific upgrade requirements such as .yo-rc.json changes, css-loader addition, resolutions/overrides entries, src/index.ts removal, and .gitignore updates for heft output directories.
constraints.mitigation: Mitigate by ensuring grounding content (skills or docs) is comprehensive and up-to-date for recent framework versions. The proposed 'spfx-upgrade' skill directly addresses this by providing all version-specific knowledge the model lacks. Additionally, the post-upgrade validation instructions help the agent detect gaps even when it cannot predict them from training data. For future SPFx releases, update the skill promptly so the agent never depends solely on base model knowledge or external documentation.

create.proposal: Create a profile-level instruction (copilot-instructions.md or equivalent) with a 'Version Fidelity' rule: 'When the user requests a specific version (e.g., v1.22.0), all dependency versions, configuration values, and generated code must target exactly that version. If external documentation or tool output references a different version, prefer the user-specified version. Flag any discrepancy to the user before proceeding. Before marking the task complete, grep all modified files for version strings and confirm they match the user's target.'
create.rationale: This is a lightweight, broadly applicable guardrail that complements the SPFx skill. It protects against ToolOutputOverWeighting across all version-upgrade scenarios (not just SPFx), ensuring the agent treats user intent as the ground truth when documentation conflicts. It would have directly prevented the v1.22.1 adoption in this run.

constraints.description: ToolOutputOverWeighting: The model treats concrete values (version numbers, package names) from fetched tool/web content as more authoritative than the user's explicit instructions. When the Microsoft Learn migration guide returned packages at v1.22.1, the model adopted those versions despite the user clearly requesting v1.22.0. This is a known model-level bias where structured, specific data from tool responses overrides vaguer user instructions, especially when the tool content appears comprehensive and authoritative.
constraints.mitigation: Layer multiple defenses: (1) The anti-hallucination skill fix (priority 2) adds explicit user-intent-anchoring instructions. (2) The SPFx upgrade skill (priority 3) removes the need to fetch external docs for version data entirely, eliminating the conflicting signal. (3) The version-fidelity instruction (priority 2) adds a pre-completion verification step. Together these reduce the model's exposure to conflicting version data and add checkpoints where the discrepancy would be caught. Long-term, model-level improvements to instruction-following fidelity (preferring explicit user requests over incidental values in tool output) would address this systemically.

rootCauses.behaviorChain: CLI output presented ESLint rule changes as separate ADD (at line 14:7) and REMOVE (at line 291:9) findings (FN025002-FN025005). rootCauses.evidence: Step 7 observation shows FN025002: 'Add override rule @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name' at File: [.eslintrc.js:14:7]. rootCauses.source: Claude Sonnet 4.6 model
rootCauses.behaviorChain: The model failed to correctly interpret the positional file:line:column references in the CLI output as distinct insertion/deletion points. It treated separate ADD and REMOVE instructions for related rules as a single in-place rename operation, likely because the model's heuristic was to minimize changes rather than precisely follow the line-number-based instructions from the CLI tool.
rootCauses.evidence: Step 37: agent replaced '@microsoft/spfx/import-requires-chunk-name': 1 and '@microsoft/spfx/pair-react-dom-render-unmount': 1 at their existing location (line ~291) with '@rushstack/' versions, instead of adding at line 14:7 as specified by FN025002/FN025003 and removing from line 291 as specified by FN025004/FN025005.

fix.behaviorChain: CLI output presented ESLint rule changes as separate ADD (at line 14:7) and REMOVE (at line 291:9) findings without explicitly indicating they are paired move operations. Agent collapsed them into a single rename-in-place at line 291, failing 2 evaluation criteria.
fix.fixTarget: m365 spfx project upgrade CLI output format (FN025002-FN025005)
fix.description: Modify the m365 CLI 'spfx project upgrade' output to explicitly group related ADD/REMOVE findings as MOVE operations, e.g., 'MOVE rule @microsoft/spfx/import-requires-chunk-name FROM .eslintrc.js:291:9 TO .eslintrc.js:14:7 (renamed to @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name)'. This eliminates ambiguity about whether ADD and REMOVE are independent or paired, and makes the positional semantics unambiguous for LLM consumers.

create.gap: No profile instructions guide the agent on interpreting positional file:line:column references in m365 CLI output as distinct, separate operations rather than heuristic rename-in-place
create.behaviorChain: Agent received CLI output with ADD at .eslintrc.js:14:7 and REMOVE at .eslintrc.js:291:9 for related rules. Without explicit guidance, agent applied a minimize-changes heuristic and renamed in-place at 291 instead of performing two distinct file edits at the specified positions.
create.proposal: Add profile instructions: 'When processing m365 spfx project upgrade output, treat each finding as an independent, literal file operation. ADD at file:line:col means INSERT content at exactly that position. REMOVE at file:line:col means DELETE content at exactly that position. Never combine an ADD and REMOVE into a single rename-in-place operation, even if the rule names appear related. Execute each finding separately at its specified location.'
create.rationale: No existing instructions or docs in the profile address how to interpret positional CLI output. The m365 CLI is an external tool whose output format cannot be quickly changed, so profile-level instructions are the fastest mitigation to prevent the agent from applying minimize-change heuristics instead of following literal positional directives.

constraints.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 applies a minimize-changes heuristic when interpreting CLI tool output, collapsing separate ADD and REMOVE instructions for semantically related items (same rule name with different prefix) into a single in-place rename. The model does not reliably treat file:line:column references as precise, independent insertion/deletion coordinates when the semantic content suggests the operations are related.
constraints.mitigation: Add explicit profile instructions reinforcing literal interpretation of positional references (see 'create' recommendation). Additionally, consider using '--output json' instead of '--output md' with the m365 CLI to provide structured data that the model can parse programmatically rather than interpreting prose-formatted findings. A post-processing step that decomposes the CLI output into an ordered list of atomic file edits (one per finding, with explicit before/after content) would further reduce model interpretation errors.

create.behaviorChain: Agent sent correct npm i -DE command for 11 devDependencies -> received exit code 0 -> assumed success without verification -> never read package.json -> 7 devDependency criteria fail
create.proposal: Create an instructions extension point titled spfx-npm-verification that specifies: (1) After any npm install command, read package.json to verify all requested packages appear at correct versions, (2) If packages are missing, check npm warnings/errors in terminal output, (3) For unavailable versions, attempt alternative resolution strategies (--legacy-peer-deps, install individually, check registry availability), (4) Never mark npm tasks complete without package.json confirmation.
create.rationale: No existing extension point covers post-install verification. The agent had no guidance to distrust exit code 0 for npm operations that may silently fail to install some packages. This is specific enough to SPFx upgrade workflows to warrant dedicated instructions.

create.gap: No skill exists to handle npm pkg set overrides syntax and verify overrides configuration in package.json
create.behaviorChain: CLI output specified npm pkg set overrides.@rushstack/heft=1.1.2 -> agent executed command -> terminal reported success -> agent did not verify overrides section exists in package.json -> criteria fails
create.proposal: Create an instructions extension point titled spfx-package-overrides that specifies: (1) npm pkg set overrides.X=Y requires correct dot-notation syntax and may behave differently across npm versions, (2) After running npm pkg set overrides commands, always read package.json to confirm an overrides key exists with the expected entries, (3) If overrides section is missing, manually edit package.json to add the overrides object, (4) Note that projects using yarn/pnpm may need resolutions instead of overrides.
create.rationale: npm pkg set overrides is a less common npm subcommand with version-dependent behavior. The agent executed it but had no way to know it might fail silently or require a different syntax for the project npm version.

create.behaviorChain: CLI output specified adding @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name: 1 to .eslintrc.js -> agent applied multi_replace_string_in_file -> tool reported success -> rule not actually present in correct location -> criteria fails
create.proposal: Create a docs extension point titled spfx-eslint-configuration that documents: (1) SPFx .eslintrc.js files often have multiple overrides sections targeting different file globs, (2) New rules must be added to the correct overrides section (typically the one matching *.ts files), (3) After editing .eslintrc.js, always read the file back to verify the rule appears in the expected location, (4) Provide example of correct rule placement in SPFx eslint override structure.
create.rationale: The agent used a string replacement tool that reported success but the rule was not placed correctly. SPFx eslint configs are complex multi-section files where naive string matching can target the wrong section. Documentation would help the agent understand the file structure before editing.

constraints.description: Model lacks inherent behavior to verify npm operations completed successfully when terminal reports exit code 0. The model treats successful exit codes as definitive proof of operation completion, but npm can exit 0 while silently failing to install packages (unavailable versions, peer dependency conflicts resolved by skipping).
constraints.mitigation: Address via profile instructions (see fix and create items above) that explicitly mandate post-command verification. Additionally, consider adding a custom MCP tool or skill that wraps npm install with automatic package.json diff verification, returning a structured success/failure report rather than relying on exit codes alone.

However, the agent made 39 get_terminal_output calls (steps 22-58, 56.9% of the trajectory) polling for npm install completion. rootCauses.label: StaleTrainingData
rootCauses.source: Model inability to properly wait for async terminal notification
rootCauses.behaviorChain: Agent ran npm install (step 21) -> command moved to background -> agent polled get_terminal_output 39 times (steps 22-58) despite acknowledging auto-notification exists -> consumed 56.9% of trajectory steps and ~4.4M prompt tokens on redundant polling
rootCauses.evidence: At step 30 the agent states 'The install is still running. I'll wait for the automatic notification when it completes.' but immediately makes another get_terminal_output call and continues polling for 28 more steps. This is a model-level inability to stop polling despite knowing the correct behavior.

fix.behaviorChain: Agent ran npm install (step 21) -> command moved to background -> agent polled get_terminal_output 39 times (steps 22-58) despite acknowledging auto-notification exists -> consumed 56.9% of trajectory steps and ~4.4M prompt tokens on redundant polling
fix.fixTarget: get_terminal_output tool description/documentation
fix.description: Add explicit anti-polling directive to the get_terminal_output tool description: 'IMPORTANT: Do NOT call this tool repeatedly to check if a command has finished. You will receive an automatic notification when background commands complete. After a command moves to the background, proceed with other available work immediately. Calling this tool more than once without receiving new output is wasteful and unnecessary.' Also add a rate-limit note: 'If you have already called this tool and received no new output, do NOT call it again until you receive a completion notification.'

create.gap: No profile-level instruction exists to guide the agent on async command handling and work continuation
create.behaviorChain: Agent ran npm install -> correctly identified it should wait for notification -> but had no instruction to continue with other preparatory work (e.g., reviewing upgrade report, planning file edits) while waiting -> wasted 39 steps polling
create.proposal: Add a profile instruction: 'When a terminal command moves to background execution (e.g., npm install, builds), DO NOT poll for completion. You will be automatically notified. Instead, immediately continue with other available work such as: reviewing documentation, planning next steps, editing files that do not depend on the running command, or reading the upgrade report output. Never make more than one get_terminal_output call after a command backgrounds without receiving a completion notification.'
create.rationale: No existing profile instruction addresses async command behavior. The agent had correct knowledge ('I'll wait for the automatic notification') but no explicit instruction reinforcing that it must stop and do other work. A profile instruction would provide a stronger behavioral anchor than relying solely on tool-level documentation, especially given the model's demonstrated tendency to override its own stated intentions.

constraints.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 exhibits compulsive polling behavior for background terminal commands despite explicitly acknowledging that auto-notification exists and that it should wait. The model states the correct behavior ('I'll wait for the automatic notification') but immediately contradicts itself by making another polling call, repeating this pattern 39 times. This represents a model-level inability to suppress action-taking impulses in favor of waiting, likely rooted in training data patterns where polling was the correct strategy.
constraints.mitigation: Layer multiple deterrents: (1) Strengthen get_terminal_output tool description with anti-polling language and explicit 'do not call more than once' directive. (2) Add profile-level instructions mandating work continuation after background commands. (3) Consider harness-level intervention: if get_terminal_output is called more than 2 times consecutively with no new output, return an error message stating 'Command still running. You will be notified on completion. Do not call this tool again until notified.' This artificial feedback loop may break the polling cycle where instructions alone cannot.

behaviorObservations.sourceArtifact: m365 spfx project upgrade JSONL output
behaviorObservations.evidence: All 30 criteria passed and all gates (select, build, run) passed. However, the trajectory consumed 125 steps total with ~80 steps (64%) spent on redundant terminal output polling during npm install/uninstall operations (steps 26-121). The agent repeatedly called get_terminal_output and read_file on terminal output files while waiting for npm commands to complete, instead of using a more efficient waiting strategy.

rootCauses.label: HumanOnlySurface
rootCauses.source: VS Code terminal interaction model requiring repeated polling for long-running npm commands
rootCauses.behaviorChain: Agent correctly invoked CLI and consumed output -> applied all file changes efficiently (steps 14-25) -> ran npm install commands which triggered long-running operations -> agent had no way to asynchronously wait for completion -> resorted to repeated get_terminal_output polling (43 calls) and read_file on large terminal output files (37 calls) -> massive step overhead but correct final result
rootCauses.evidence: Steps 26-121 show the agent calling get_terminal_output and read_file repeatedly in pairs, seeing output like 'npm warn EBADENGINE' and 'npm warn deprecated' without a completion signal, then calling again. The agent explicitly says 'I'll wait for the npm install to finish' (step 39), 'Still running' (step 44), 'I'll keep waiting' (step 41) showing it was blocked by the terminal interaction model.

fix.behaviorChain: Agent ran npm install/uninstall commands individually -> each triggered long-running operations -> agent polled get_terminal_output repeatedly (43 calls) and read_file on terminal output (37 calls) -> 64% of trajectory steps wasted on polling
fix.fixTarget: Profile instructions for VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat
fix.description: Add profile instructions directing the agent to batch all npm install operations into a single command (e.g., 'npm install pkg1 pkg2 pkg3') and all npm uninstall operations into a single command, rather than running them individually. Also instruct the agent to use '--legacy-peer-deps' flag to avoid engine warning loops that extend output without signaling completion. This reduces the number of long-running terminal operations from many to 2-3, dramatically cutting polling overhead.

create.gap: No instructions exist to guide the agent on efficient terminal polling strategy for long-running commands in VS Code
create.behaviorChain: Agent had no guidance on how to handle long-running terminal commands -> defaulted to rapid repeated polling of get_terminal_output -> could not distinguish between 'still running' and 'completed with warnings' states -> wasted 80+ steps on redundant polling
create.proposal: Create profile instructions that specify: (1) after issuing a long-running command like npm install, wait at least 15-30 seconds between get_terminal_output polls; (2) look for specific completion indicators ('added X packages', 'up to date', 'npm error', shell prompt return) rather than polling until output stops changing; (3) combine dependency changes into minimal npm commands before executing.
create.rationale: No existing extension point provides guidance on terminal polling cadence or completion detection heuristics. The agent's correct behavior (it eventually succeeded) shows it understands the task, but lacks strategy guidance for the polling interaction model. Instructions are the appropriate type since this is behavioral guidance, not a tool gap.

constraints.description: VS Code terminal interaction model via get_terminal_output MCP tool provides no asynchronous completion notification or blocking wait mechanism. The agent must repeatedly poll for output and infer command completion from output patterns, with no explicit 'process exited' signal. This is inherent to the VS Code extension terminal API surface.
constraints.mitigation: Profile-level mitigations: (1) Instruct agent to batch npm operations to minimize number of long-running commands. (2) Instruct agent to append '&& echo DONE' to commands so it can detect a clear completion marker. (3) Instruct agent to use longer polling intervals (20-30s) for known long-running operations like npm install. Harness-level mitigation (external): enhance get_terminal_output tool to accept a 'wait_for_exit' parameter or emit a completion event when the shell process returns to idle.
